# R8 Digest — Escapes through Gilboa 23–31 (13417–16224)
**Source:** Tsumura, *The First Book of Samuel* (NICOT, 2006)
**Reader:** extraction subagent R8
**Coverage:** slice `R8_escape_gilboa_23-31_13417-16224.txt` read in full (raw lines **13417–16224** ≈ slice L1–L2808; NICOT pp. ~549–656). Philological/text-critical minutiae sparsely noted; narrative-theological and Endor/Gilboa material extracted fully.

## Claims

### C-R8-01 | Keilah: David inquires of Yahweh before Abiathar arrives
- **Claim (attributed Tsumura):** Locals inform David of Philistine attack on Keilah (plundering threshing floors). David inquires of the Lord (presumably via Gad or exceptional spirit-speech; Abiathar not yet with him at 23:1–4). Too much emphasis has been put on Abiathar’s arrival as if only then the oracle becomes David’s ally—David already sought God’s will (22:15) and was guided by Yahweh before Abiathar.
- **Quote:** “Too much emphasis has been given on Abiathar’s arrival as if ‘the divine oracle is now David’s ally to guide him into safety.’” / “David received advice from Yahweh through the prophet and the priest as well as information from the local people. On the other hand, Saul’s only help was from local informants”
- **Locus:** 23:1–4; pp. 549–551 / slice ~L1–L62
- **Targets:** [[1-samuel]], [[david]], [[saul]], [[divine-providence]], [[david-tsumura]]

### C-R8-02 | Keilah geography and double inquiry; battle is the Lord’s
- **Claim:** Keilah ≈ Khirbet Qîlā (MR 150–113), ~3 mi S of Adullam, near Philistine border; “here in Judah” (23:3) implies Keilah not then within Judahite limits. Second inquiry (23:4) is deliberate reassurance (cf. Gideon Judg 6:36–40). David not silenced by men’s fear; “the battle is the Lord’s” (cf. 17:47).
- **Quote:** “Regardless of human conditions God can still use the works of David and his men, for the battle is the Lord’s (see 1 Sam. 17:47).”
- **Locus:** 23:1–5; pp. 550–552 / ~L42–L74
- **Targets:** [[1-samuel]], [[david]], [[philistines]]

### C-R8-03 | Abiathar + ephod at Keilah; Urim-type yes/no
- **Claim:** Parenthetical 23:6: Abiathar flees to David *at Keilah* with ephod—MT need not be a gloss; 22:20 did not state where David was. With ephod David has “a more sure means of ascertaining the will of Yahweh”; answers in 23:11–12 are yes/no type (Urim/Thummim assumed).
- **Quote:** “In Keilah, with Abiathar and the oracular ephod… David has now ‘a more sure means of ascertaining the will of Yahweh.’”
- **Locus:** 23:6–12; pp. 552–555 / ~L79–L147
- **Targets:** [[1-samuel]], [[david]]

### C-R8-04 | Saul misjudges “God has alienated him”; Keilah would betray David
- **Claim:** Saul thinks God has delivered/alienated David into his hand because Keilah has doors and bar—wrong conviction. Citizens of Keilah will deliver David up (oracle): ungrateful but rational after Nob; Philistines only went after grain, Saul would destroy the city.
- **Quote:** “Saul’s belief that God was on his side turns out to be wrong. Without God’s help and guidance we can certainly misjudge a situation”
- **Locus:** 23:7–13; pp. 553–556 / ~L88–L234
- **Targets:** [[saul]], [[david]], [[1-samuel]]

### C-R8-05 | Wilderness of Ziph: God did not give David into Saul’s hand
- **Claim:** 23:14 theological summary: Saul sought day after day, “but God did not give him into his hand.” Lord with David. Ziph ≈ Tell Zîp, ~5 mi SSE of Hebron.
- **Quote:** “With (but God) the narrator contrasts Saul and God, summing up the theological deduction… the Lord was with David, and so God did not give him into Saul’s hand.”
- **Locus:** 23:14; pp. 556–557 / ~L235–L249
- **Targets:** [[david]], [[saul]], [[divine-providence]], [[1-samuel]]

### C-R8-06 | Jonathan at Horesh: last meeting; covenant renewed; David will be king
- **Claim:** Jonathan comes to Horesh, encourages David “by God” (unique addition to *ḥzq yādô*). Explicitly accepts David will be king, himself *mišneh* (second-in-command). Renews covenant before the Lord. Last recorded meeting; next mention is Gilboa death (31:2; 2 Sam 1:4). Saul already “knows so” (confirmed 24:21).
- **Quote:** “This is the last recorded meeting of Jonathan with David.” / “he expects ‘nothing more for himself than the position of second-in-command’”
- **Locus:** 23:15–18; pp. 557–559 / ~L252–L289
- **Targets:** [[jonathan]], [[david]], [[saul]], [[kingship-in-israel]], [[1-samuel]]

### C-R8-07 | Ziphites inform Saul; Crag of the Divisions — providential Philistine raid
- **Claim:** Ziphites (Judahite) betray David’s location (Hachilah/Jeshimon; Ps 54 title). Saul nearly surrounds David in wilderness of Maon; messenger reports Philistine raid; place named *selaʿ hammaḥleqôt* “Crag of the Divisions.” Tsumura: God divided David and Saul providentially; “Behind all these ‘happenings’ one can certainly recognize God’s strong hand.”
- **Quote:** “At the right moment, a messenger came providentially, although as if by chance.” / “the rock was named after this incident in which God divided David and Saul providentially.”
- **Locus:** 23:19–28; pp. 559–562 / ~L290–L436
- **Targets:** [[david]], [[saul]], [[philistines]], [[divine-providence]], [[1-samuel]]

### C-R8-08 | Hinge to En-gedi (23:29/24:1)
- **Claim:** Transitional hinge: David lives in strongholds of En-gedi (“spring of the young goat”; ʿAin Jidi), oasis/caves on Dead Sea W shore. Prefer hinge (A/ab/B) reading of verse-division traditions.
- **Quote:** “Being an oasis, it was a good place for a temporary refuge, and there were caves in the vicinity”
- **Locus:** 23:29; p. 563 / ~L437–L443
- **Targets:** [[david]], [[1-samuel]]

### C-R8-09 | Ch. 24 apologetic: Did David wrest the throne by violence? No
- **Claim:** Episode answers “Did David attempt to wrest the throne from Saul by violence?” negatively. Apologetic vs charges like Shimei’s (2 Sam 16:8) that David is guilty of blood of Saul’s house; document likely from David’s reign era. Chs 24–26 shift: David from life endangered to one who spares life.
- **Quote:** “this episode answers the question, ‘Did David attempt to wrest the throne from Saul by violence?’ in the negative, ‘No.’”
- **Locus:** 24 intro; pp. 563–564 / ~L444–L449
- **Targets:** [[david]], [[saul]], [[kingship-in-israel]], [[1-samuel]], [[tsumura-1-samuel-nicot]]

### C-R8-10 | Cave: cut skirt, heart struck; refuse to strike LORD’s anointed
- **Claim:** Saul enters cave “to cover his legs” (euphemism for defecation); David’s men claim God-given day to kill enemy; David cuts skirt of robe secretly then heart strikes him (cutting hem = disloyalty/rebellion symbol in 2nd-mill. practice). Refuses: “Lord forbid… to the Lord’s anointed (*mešîaḥ YHWH*)… he is anointed of the Lord.” Disagrees with men; does not permit rise against Saul. Saul still “anointed” though spirit left (16:14)—sacrosanct.
- **Quote:** “David respected Saul as the Lord’s anointed… even though the spirit of the Lord had already left him (16:14).” / “The anointed of the Lord should not be killed or even cursed (26:9, 11, 16, 23; 2 Sam. 1:14, 16; 19:21).”
- **Locus:** 24:1–7; pp. 564–568 / ~L450–L521
- **Targets:** [[david]], [[saul]], [[kingship-in-israel]], [[1-samuel]]

### C-R8-11 | David’s speech: leave vengeance to Yahweh; proverb; flea/dead dog
- **Claim:** David appeals: Lord gave Saul into hand but he would not stretch hand against anointed; “May the Lord judge… avenge me… my hand shall not be on you.” Ancient proverb: “Out of the wicked comes forth wickedness” = deeds express dispositions. Self-abasement as dead dog / single flea. Unlike Macbeth, firm against “helping” God along.
- **Quote:** “David here as in 26:10 leaves his vengeance to the Lord… unlike Macbeth, he was firm against the temptation to ‘help’ God along.”
- **Locus:** 24:8–15; pp. 568–571 / ~L522–L615
- **Targets:** [[david]], [[saul]], [[divine-providence]], [[1-samuel]]

### C-R8-12 | Saul’s response: you more righteous; you will be king; oath for seed
- **Claim:** Saul weeps (self-pity more than repentance), “You are more righteous than I,” admits David will “surely become king” and kingdom established in his hand; exacts oath not to cut off seed/name. David swears; parties separate. Birch’s “climactic moment of David’s rise” problem: nothing seems to come of this moment.
- **Quote:** “Saul finally admits (now, I know) that David will surely become king… as Jonathan had already acknowledged.”
- **Locus:** 24:16–22; pp. 571–574 / ~L616–L678
- **Targets:** [[saul]], [[david]], [[kingship-in-israel]], [[1-samuel]]

### C-R8-13 | Samuel’s death (25:1); David to wilderness of Paran
- **Claim:** Samuel dies; all Israel laments and buries him in his house in Ramah. With his passing no reconciliation path for David and Saul; David goes further south. MT *Pāʾrān* lectio difficilior vs LXX “Maon”; if stronghold=Masada area, Paran south end of Arabah possible. Burial in house unusual in Israel; Ugaritic parallel noted but Israelite ancestor-worship of Samuel unlikely.
- **Quote:** “With his passing there is no way David and Saul can be reconciled.”
- **Locus:** 25:1; pp. 574–575 / ~L680–L705
- **Targets:** [[1-samuel]], [[david]], [[saul]]
- **Misc flag:** Samuel death intercalation

### C-R8-14 | Ch. 25 sandwiched: vengeance the Lord’s not David’s; Abigail restrains
- **Claim:** Abigail/Nabal episode between two spare-Saul chapters; same issue—will vengeance be David’s or the Lord’s? In 24 David desires Lord avenge Saul; here God avenges speedily (v. 39); in 26 David more specific God will avenge (26:10). Difference: here *David* wants vengeance and another’s words pull him back. Abigail *ʾēšet ḥayil* points error of ways. Marriage to Calebite widow builds Hebron power base without planning—God’s unseen hand (Rom 8:28). Motive ≠ Uriah/Bathsheba (not cover-up adultery).
- **Quote:** “Taking his own revenge would make him unfit to carry out God’s mission for him (25:30–31).” / “God’s unseen hand of guidance is clearly recognizable”
- **Locus:** 25 intro; pp. 575–576 / ~L706–L713
- **Targets:** [[david]], [[divine-providence]], [[kingship-in-israel]], [[1-samuel]]
- **Misc flag:** Abigail, Nabal — substantial

### C-R8-15 | Nabal and Abigail character contrast; Calebite
- **Claim:** Nabal of Maon, business/sheep-shearing at Carmel (Judah; not Mt Carmel); very rich (3000 sheep, 1000 goats). Name *nābāl* = foolish/senseless (BDB); Levenson: may not be real name but character-label—possible unproven. Abigail: good intelligence and beautiful; Nabal coarse/ill-behaved, Calebite (clan status and/or “dog”-type roughness).
- **Quote:** “The woman was of good intelligence and beautiful in appearance, but the man was coarse and ill-behaved; he was a Calebite”
- **Locus:** 25:2–3; pp. 576–577 / ~L714–L729
- **Targets:** [[1-samuel]], [[david]]
- **Misc flag:** Abigail, Nabal

### C-R8-16 | David’s request, Nabal’s contempt, David girds for slaughter
- **Claim:** David sends ten young men for feast-day provisions after protecting Nabal’s shepherds (“wall night and day”). Nabal: “Who is David?… many servants break away”—formal rejection of covenant-invitation (Wiseman); speaks like later rebels (2 Sam 20:1). David arms ~400 men (200 with baggage)—attack almost unavoidable.
- **Quote:** “Nabal speaks like one of the later rebels against Davidic rule… and therein, from the viewpoint of the narrative, lies his real fault.”
- **Locus:** 25:4–13; pp. 577–582 / ~L730–L844
- **Targets:** [[david]], [[1-samuel]]
- **Misc flag:** Nabal

### C-R8-17 | Abigail’s intervention: bloodguilt, enduring house, Document of the Living
- **Claim:** Servant informs Abigail; she loads substantial gift (list compared to Papyrus Anastasi I field rations). Meets David providentially (“Right at that moment… not by chance”). Parenthetical flashback: David’s oath to wipe out every “wall-pisser” (all males)—overreaction; needs God’s intervention via Abigail. Speech: Nabal lives up to name; Lord withheld David from bloodguilt and self-won victory; gift; Lord will make *bayit neʾĕmān* (enduring house; Nathan/2 Sam 7 trajectory); life tied in *ṣĕrôr haḥayyîm* (prefers “Document of the Living” / Book of Living, Tur-Sinai, over “bundle of life”); when appointed *nāgîd* over Israel, no tottering/stumbling heart from vain bloodshed. Avoiding bloodguilt key to future kingship (contrast Bathsheba blood-guilt later).
- **Quote:** “the Lord withheld you from entering into bloodguilt and gaining victory for yourself with your own hand.” / “Without God’s grace, no one can be not only forgiven of his past sins but also protected from committing further sins.”
- **Locus:** 25:14–31; pp. 582–591 / ~L845–L1179
- **Targets:** [[david]], [[kingship-in-israel]], [[divine-providence]], [[1-samuel]]
- **Misc flag:** Abigail (wise woman type; cf. Tekoa, Abel)

### C-R8-18 | David blesses Yahweh/Abigail; Nabal struck by the Lord
- **Claim:** David: Blessed be Lord who sent Abigail; blessed her judgment for preventing bloodguilt. Takes gift; “lifted up your face.” Nabal king-like banquet, drunk; next day heart dies (stroke → “became a stone”); in ~10 days “the Lord struck Nabal and he died.” David: Lord conducted case of insult; withheld servant from evil; turned Nabal’s evil on his head. Foreshadow: Lord will eventually strike Saul too.
- **Quote:** “It is stated that ‘the Lord struck Nabal.’ One may assume that the Lord will eventually strike Saul too.”
- **Locus:** 25:32–39a; pp. 591–593 / ~L1180–L1249
- **Targets:** [[david]], [[saul]], [[divine-providence]], [[1-samuel]]
- **Misc flag:** Nabal death; Abigail

### C-R8-19 | Abigail marries David; Ahinoam; Michal given to Palti
- **Claim:** David marries Abigail (mother of Chileab/Daniel; probably died young). Also Ahinoam of Jezreel (Judah)—mother of Amnon; likely married first; political steps toward throne. Saul gives Michal to Palti of Gallim to weaken David politically; David can reclaim her later (2 Sam 3). Hand of Lord working for good.
- **Quote:** “David’s marriages to Ahinoam and Abigail were possibly politically motivated: they were decisive steps on the way to the throne.”
- **Locus:** 25:39b–44; pp. 593–594 / ~L1250–L1286
- **Targets:** [[david]], [[saul]], [[kingship-in-israel]], [[1-samuel]]
- **Misc flag:** Abigail, Ahinoam, Michal

### C-R8-20 | Ch. 26 vs 24: similar outline, two distinct occasions
- **Claim:** Many treat 24 and 26 as variants of one story; Koch’s six-point outline of similarities. Tsumura: similarities overemphasized; basic differences (En-gedi vs Ziph; Saul alone vs with Abner/soldiers; skirt vs spear+water jar; Saul acknowledges future kingship vs only blesses success; speech structure differs). Similarities show nature of David–Saul relation; differences show two distinct occasions. Last encounter; after this David leaves territory of Israel (27:1).
- **Quote:** “the differences show that there were two distinct occasions when David acted similarly toward Saul.” / “This is the last encounter between David and Saul.”
- **Locus:** 26 intro; pp. 594–596 / ~L1287–L1326
- **Targets:** [[david]], [[saul]], [[1-samuel]], [[tsumura-1-samuel-nicot]]

### C-R8-21 | Hachilah night raid: deep sleep from the Lord; refuse anointed again
- **Claim:** Ziphites again inform (with article—same group as 23:19). Saul camps with 3000 chosen. David and Abishai enter camp; Abishai offers to pin Saul with spear—“God has delivered.” David: Do not destroy; who stretched hand against Lord’s anointed and is still innocent? Lord will strike him (day comes / dies in war)—thinking of Nabal experience. Takes spear and water jar. “Deep sleep from the Lord” (*tardēmat YHWH*) on camp—divine aid (cf. Gen 2:21; 15:12; Isa 29:10).
- **Quote:** “As the Lord lives, the Lord himself will surely strike him, whether his day comes and he dies or he goes down into war and perishes!” / “a deep sleep from the Lord had fallen upon them.”
- **Locus:** 26:1–12; pp. 596–601 / ~L1327–L1531
- **Targets:** [[david]], [[saul]], [[divine-providence]], [[kingship-in-israel]], [[1-samuel]]
- **Misc flag:** Abishai, Abner first major stage appearance

### C-R8-22 | David rebukes Abner; inheritance of the Lord; flea/partridge
- **Claim:** From mountain distance David shames Abner for failing to watch “your lord, the Lord’s anointed”—you (pl.) are *benê-māwet*. To Saul: if Lord instigated, accept offering; if men, curse them—for driving David from *naḥălat YHWH* (land + covenant people) saying “Go, serve other gods!” (limitation of *worship* location, not of YHWH’s power—chs 4–6 etc.). Wordplay *qōrēʾ* caller/partridge. Saul: “I have sinned… acted foolishly”—David sensibly ignores promise (→27:1). David trusts Lord’s return of righteousness/faithfulness; will not send hand into anointed. Saul blesses success; last meeting.
- **Quote:** “to chase David away from the Lord’s inheritance… is a capital offense against the Lord of Israel” / “he will never see him again.”
- **Locus:** 26:13–25; pp. 602–607 / ~L1532–L1695
- **Targets:** [[david]], [[saul]], [[kingship-in-israel]], [[1-samuel]]

### C-R8-23 | Philistia sojourn: last resort, apologetic tone, not duplicate of 21:11–16
- **Claim:** Chs 27–30 Ziklag sojourn interrupted by Endor (28:3–25). Highly apologetic: went only as last resort; in Achish’s service attacked Israel’s enemies not Israel. Reports ingenuity in hostile circumstances; learned Philistine military/admin technique (Philistine culture advanced). 27 ≠ secondary “corrective” of 21: alone/madman trick vs formal service with 600 + families; “duping of Achish” only common thin link. Possible Achish as official appellation (Ekron “Akhayus”); Ben-Maoch may distinguish persons (cf. Pharaoh + name).
- **Quote:** “although David did enter the service of a Philistine king, he was merely using the opportunity to acquire a base of operations from which to fight other enemies of Israel.” (McCarter’s framing, which Tsumura partly accepts as report of ingenuity)
- **Locus:** 27 intro–2; pp. 607–610 / ~L1696–L1747
- **Targets:** [[david]], [[philistines]], [[1-samuel]], [[tsumura-1-samuel-nicot]]
- **Misc flag:** Achish / Achish Ben-Maoch

### C-R8-24 | Ziklag grant; raids; deception of Achish; eternal servant
- **Claim:** David asks for provincial city; Achish gives Ziklag—belonged to kings of Judah “to this day” (editorial; Halpern: fits ~10th c. / pre-Shishaq settlement pattern). Stay: year and four months. Raids Geshurites, Gezerites(?), Amalekites toward Shur/Egypt; leaves no survivors so they cannot inform; tells Achish he raided Negeb of Judah/Jerahmeelites/Kenites. Achish trusts: David “utterly abhorred” among Israel → *ʿebed ʿôlām* (eternal servant/lifelong slave; Ugaritic *ʿbd ʿlm*).
- **Quote:** “And Achish trusted David, saying, ‘He has become utterly abhorred among his people Israel! And he will become an eternal servant to me!’”
- **Locus:** 27:5–12; pp. 610–614 / ~L1748–L1820
- **Targets:** [[david]], [[philistines]], [[1-samuel]]
- **Misc flag:** Achish, Ziklag

### C-R8-25 | Philistines gather; Achish appoints David bodyguard (28:1–2)
- **Claim:** Philistines gather for war; Achish: you march with me. David’s ambiguous “you will know what your servant can do”; Achish appoints him lifelong bodyguard (*šōmēr lerōʾšî*). Tense dialogue marked by repeated “X said to Y.”
- **Quote:** “Then I will appoint you as my bodyguard for life!”
- **Locus:** 28:1–2; pp. 614–615 / ~L1821–L1847
- **Targets:** [[david]], [[philistines]], [[1-samuel]]

### C-R8-26 | Endor placement: AXBY dischronology, not Deuteronomistic excision accident
- **Claim:** 28:3–25 chronologically follows ch. 30 (Philistines already at Shunem/Gilboa vs still at Aphek in 29:1). Not best explained as removed for Deut 18 offense then reinserted wrong. Sophisticated *dischronologization*: organizing principle is dramatis personae (Saul/David), not army geography. Pattern **AXBY**: David 28:1–2 (A) → 29–30 (B); Saul 28:3–25 (X) → 31 (Y). Overall: last Gilboa battle initiated by Philistines with whom David associated, but David did not participate; Saul/sons/army perish.
- **Quote:** “the narrator alternates the episodes centered on David and those centered on Saul.” / “David did not participate in the battle.”
- **Locus:** 28 placement discussion; pp. 615–617 / ~L1848–L1907
- **Targets:** [[1-samuel]], [[david]], [[saul]], [[philistines]], [[tsumura-1-samuel-nicot]]

### C-R8-27 | Endor: not support for God using pagan necromancy as normal channel
- **Claim:** Story depicts futility of conjuring the dead—results in announcement of death; “to speak with the dead is to join the dead.” Does *not* support view that God sometimes uses pagan practice for his purpose. Rather, something unusual even to the necromancer occurred through God’s power; *situation* used to declare judgment on Saul. Later condemned (1 Chr 10:13). Not ancestor worship (Samuel not Saul’s ancestor). Briefer/less elaborate than Mesopotamian necromancy texts.
- **Quote:** “this story does not support a view that God sometimes uses even the pagan religious practice for his own purpose. Rather, something very unusual even from the perspective of the female necromancer occurred through God’s power.”
- **Locus:** 28 intro; pp. 616–617 / ~L1905–L1909
- **Targets:** [[saul]], [[1-samuel]], [[divine-providence]], [[tsumura-1-samuel-nicot]]
- **Misc flag:** medium of Endor — substantial

### C-R8-28 | Five technical verbs for inquiry modes (Endor)
- **Claim:** Narrative carefully distinguishes: (1) *šʾl b-* (v.6) legitimate “inquire of” God (dreams/Urim/prophets); (2) *drš b-* (v.7) “seek through” medium/ghosts—never priests-to-God; (3) *qrʾ l-* (v.15) “invoke” (Ugaritic *qrʾ* for dead *rpum*); (4) *qsm b-* (v.8) “divine by”—illicit complex (Deut 18:14); (5) *ʿlh* Hi (vv.8,11) “bring up” (Akk. *šūlû*, Šamaš psychopomp).
- **Quote:** “the present narrative carefully distinguishes five verbs that refer to modes by which humans inquire of the divine will”
- **Locus:** Excursus technical expressions; pp. 617–618 / ~L1910–L1935
- **Targets:** [[1-samuel]], [[saul]], [[david-tsumura]]
- **Misc flag:** medium of Endor

### C-R8-29 | Setting: Samuel dead; Saul had expelled ʾôbôt and yiddeʿōnîm
- **Claim:** Reminds of Samuel’s death/burial (25:1). Saul had driven necromancers (*ʾōbôt*) and mediums (*yiddeʿōnîm*) from land—evidence Mosaic prohibitions (Deut 18:11; Lev 19–20) operative; unlikely later editor invent good about Saul. *ʾôb*: (a) spirit of dead (≈ Akk. *eṭemmu*), not necessarily deified ancestor; (b) necromancy practice; (c) necromancer. *yiddeʿōnî* always parallel *ʾôb*, usually practitioner not spirit. Philistines encamp Shunem; Saul on Gilboa; heart fears greatly.
- **Quote:** “This verse seems to be strong evidence of the existence of the prohibition at this time as it is unlikely that a later editor would have made up something good about Saul.”
- **Locus:** 28:3–5; pp. 618–621 / ~L1936–L1971
- **Targets:** [[saul]], [[philistines]], [[1-samuel]]
- **Misc flag:** medium of Endor; ʾôb terminology

### C-R8-30 | No answer by dreams, Urim, or prophets; seeks ʾēšet baʿălat ʾôb
- **Claim:** Saul inquires (*šʾl b-*)—Lord does not answer by dreams or Urim or prophets (v.6; reason v.16: Lord turned away). Seeks “woman who serves the Lady of the ʾob-spirits” (Tsumura’s rendering of *ʾēšet baʿălat ʾôb*); found at En-dor (Khirbet eṣ-Ṣafṣafe, 4.5 mi NE of Shunem—other side of enemy camp). Disguises, goes by night with two men.
- **Quote:** “the Lord did not answer him, even by dreams or Urim or prophets.”
- **Locus:** 28:6–8a; pp. 620–622 / ~L1960–L1997
- **Targets:** [[saul]], [[1-samuel]]
- **Misc flag:** medium of Endor

### C-R8-31 | Divine by ʾôb; swear by YHWH; bring up Samuel
- **Claim:** At night (standard necromantic time; solar deity as *bēl eṭemmi* in underworld). “Divine for me by ʾob-spirits and bring up….” Woman cites Saul’s ban; Saul ironically swears “As the Lord lives! No guilt shall fall on you.” Orders Samuel brought up. No description of invoking—illicit, writer will not detail actual act.
- **Quote:** “It is certainly ironic that Saul uses this formula while seeking guidance from the spirit of the dead” / “Perhaps it is because it was so illicit that the writer did not want even to mention the actual act.”
- **Locus:** 28:8b–11; pp. 622–623 / ~L1999–L2046
- **Targets:** [[saul]], [[1-samuel]]
- **Misc flag:** medium of Endor

### C-R8-32 | Tsumura on what happens: real Samuel; extraordinary to the medium; God permitted
- **Claim:** Woman sees Samuel, shouts loud voice—discourse break (wayqtl + stated subject) before she addresses Saul suggests something unexpected outside her control. Ordinary divining powers may not have been employed; stronger power at work. Spirit may not have appeared/acted like usual *ʾôb*/*repāʾîm* she handles. “Presented as an actual event, not a dream or a vision.” Recognition of Saul possibly via spirit naming him. Author intends *really Samuel*—only he could give that message; “we have to assume that God permitted the witch to call Samuel up in this case even though he might not normally have allowed it.” Even if “you disturbed me” credits her action, message is from Yahweh.
- **Quote:** “It should be noted that Samuel’s ‘coming up from the underworld’ is ‘presented as an actual event, not a dream or a vision, even though dreams are explicitly mentioned by Saul.’” / “the author certainly intends us to believe it is really Samuel… God permitted the witch to call Samuel up in this case even though he might not normally have allowed it.”
- **Locus:** 28:12a and commentary; pp. 623–627 / ~L2028–L2139
- **Targets:** [[saul]], [[1-samuel]], [[divine-providence]], [[david-tsumura]], [[tsumura-1-samuel-nicot]]
- **Misc flag:** medium of Endor — load-bearing interpretation

### C-R8-33 | “I saw gods (ʾĕlōhîm) coming up”; old man in robe
- **Claim:** Woman: *ʾĕlōhîm ʿōlîm* (plural participle)—“gods”/spirits of dead/preternatural beings (Ugaritic *rpim—ilnym*; Gordon: slain heroes as gods of earth; cf. Isa 8:19). Saul still seeks Yahweh’s prophet: asks singular appearance. “Old man… wrapped in a robe” (*meʿîl*—Samuel’s characteristic garment 15:27; 2:19). Saul knows it is Samuel; bows—does **not** worship Samuel as deity; speaks as to living prophet; narrator also says “Samuel” not “ghost.”
- **Quote:** “Saul did not worship Samuel as a divine being when he appeared…. To Saul, Yahweh was still his only God, and Samuel spoke with Saul as the prophet of Yahweh.”
- **Locus:** 28:12b–14b; pp. 624–627 / ~L2051–L2086
- **Targets:** [[saul]], [[1-samuel]]
- **Misc flag:** medium of Endor

### C-R8-34 | Samuel’s oracle: kingdom to David; death tomorrow; Amalek sin
- **Claim:** Samuel: Why disturb (*rgz*—Sheol stirred; Phoenician tomb-violation) me? Saul: distress; Philistines fight; God turned away—no answer by prophets or dreams (Urim omitted; merism). Samuel: why inquire of me when Lord turned away and become adversary? Lord torn kingship, given to neighbor **David** (names him; ch. 15 recalled—did not execute anger on Amalek). Poetic AXB 28:19: Israel/camp into Philistine hand; “tomorrow you and your sons shall be with me” = join community of dead in Sheol (abode of righteous and rejected). Samuel uses divine name Yahweh seven times; Saul said “God” once.
- **Quote:** “tomorrow you and your sons shall be with me” / “Saul will join the community of the dead by entering the netherworld, Sheol”
- **Locus:** 28:15–19; pp. 626–628 / ~L2087–L2193
- **Targets:** [[saul]], [[david]], [[philistines]], [[kingship-in-israel]], [[1-samuel]]
- **Misc flag:** medium of Endor; full death announcement

### C-R8-35 | Saul falls full length; meal; returns to Gilboa same night
- **Claim:** Saul falls full length, terrified by words; no strength—had not eaten all day/night (purification for meeting Samuel—“very religious” yet rejected). Woman and servants urge food; he eats; they go that night. “God’s word stood and could not be altered.” He does not try to avoid next day’s battle. Fast nine-wayqtl terminus tempo.
- **Quote:** “Saul ‘did himself no good by doing what he had decreed to be unlawful. God’s word stood and could not be altered.’” / “It is to be noted that he did not try to avoid the battle the next day.”
- **Locus:** 28:20–25; pp. 628–629 / ~L2194–L2237
- **Targets:** [[saul]], [[1-samuel]]
- **Misc flag:** medium of Endor

### C-R8-36 | Excursus: ʾēšet baʿălat ʾôb = woman who serves solar “Lady of ʾôb-spirits”
- **Claim:** Rejects simple “woman who has a familiar spirit” / LXX conflation as sole solutions. Proposes objective genitive: woman who serves *baʿălat ʾôb*—“Lady of ʾôb-spirits” = sun goddess in nocturnal/infernal phase (cf. Akk. Šamaš *bēl eṭemmi*; Ugaritic Shapshu psychopomp, KTU 1.161 / Baal cycle). Popular Israelite religion may have cast solar goddess as psychopomp; she is patron of the female necromancer.
- **Quote:** “ʾēšet baʿălat ʾôb means a ‘woman who serves the Lady of the dead spirits,’ ‘the Lady’ referring to the sun goddess as ruler or guide of the spirits in the netherworld.”
- **Locus:** Excursus after 28; pp. 630–631 / ~L2240–L2267
- **Targets:** [[1-samuel]], [[david-tsumura]]
- **Misc flag:** medium of Endor; solar goddess hypothesis

### C-R8-37 | Ch. 29: Philistine lords reject David from battle — providence
- **Claim:** Resumes 28:2 (B of AXBY). Philistines assemble Aphek; Israel at spring in Jezreel (Harod). Lords: “What are these Hebrews?” Achish defends; lords angry—send him back to appointed place (Ziklag); fear he become adversary with heads of “these men” (=us); cite dancing song Saul/thousands David/ten thousands. Achish dismisses David with *ḥay-YHWH* oath (courtesy or polytheistic use of David’s god). David’s “enemies of my master the king” ambiguous—Achish or Saul. God providentially engineers so David need not fight Saul; led to Ziklag hard trial.
- **Quote:** “Here again God providentially engineers the course of David’s life by His sovereign will so that he does not have to fight against Saul.”
- **Locus:** 29:1–11; pp. 632–637 / ~L2268–L2410
- **Targets:** [[david]], [[philistines]], [[saul]], [[divine-providence]], [[1-samuel]]
- **Misc flag:** Achish

### C-R8-38 | Amalekite raid on Ziklag; David strengthens himself in the Lord
- **Claim:** Third day return: Ziklag burned; women/children taken, none killed. David’s two wives among captives. Troops speak of stoning him (bitter souls); “David strengthened himself in the Lord, his God.” Inquires via Abiathar’s ephod: pursue? overtake?—“Pursue! For you can surely overtake and rescue.”
- **Quote:** “And David strengthened himself in the Lord, his God.” / “Only the intimate relationship with his personal God gave him strength in such a critical time.”
- **Locus:** 30:1–8; pp. 637–639 / ~L2411–L2467
- **Targets:** [[david]], [[divine-providence]], [[1-samuel]]
- **Misc flag:** Ahinoam, Abigail captives

### C-R8-39 | Pursuit via Egyptian slave; total recovery; equal spoil statute
- **Claim:** 600 to Naḥal Besor (Wadi Ghazzeh?); 200 too exhausted remain. Egyptian Amalekite slave abandoned when ill—fed, guides to celebrating Amalekites. David strikes dawn to after sunset; 400 young men flee on camels. All recovered including two wives; “nothing was lacking… everything David recovered.” “This is David’s plunder!” (contrast Saul ch. 15). At Besor, evil/worthless men refuse share to rear guard; David: Lord gave victory; share of baggage-guard = battle-goer; made statute and custom for Israel “until this day.”
- **Quote:** “For the share of the one who stayed by the baggage shall be the same as the share of the one who went down to the battle; they should share together!”
- **Locus:** 30:9–25; pp. 639–646 / ~L2468–L2617
- **Targets:** [[david]], [[1-samuel]], [[kingship-in-israel]]

### C-R8-40 | Gifts to elders of Judah; Hebron trajectory; messianic prototype
- **Claim:** David sends plunder gifts to elders of Judah / neighbors—“plunder of the enemies of the Lord.” List: Bethel (Judahite), Ramoth-negeb, Jattir, Aroer, Siphmoth, Eshtemoa, Racal, Jerahmeelite and Kenite cities, Hormah, Bor-ashan, Athach, **Hebron** + all places David went around. Elders = those who anoint him king of Judah (2 Sam 2:4). List ends with Hebron → points to capital before Jerusalem. Transitional LINK outcast → Judah kingship. “Hand of the Lord working… preparing David to be the future king, the prototype of the Messiah.”
- **Quote:** “In summary, we can see the hand of the Lord working in all these matters, preparing David to be the future king, the prototype of the Messiah.”
- **Locus:** 30:26–31; pp. 646–649 / ~L2618–L2686
- **Targets:** [[david]], [[kingship-in-israel]], [[divine-providence]], [[1-samuel]]

### C-R8-41 | Gilboa: Philistines fight; sons fall; simultaneous with Amalekite pursuit
- **Claim:** 31 joins Saul line (from 28 end) and Philistine line (from 29 end). While David pursued Amalekites (*rdp* 30:8), Philistines pursue Saul (*dbq*). Israel flees, falls wounded on Mount Gilboa. Philistines strike Jonathan, Abinadab, Malchishua—three sons die per Samuel 28:19. Ishbosheth and Abner escape (→2 Sam 2:8).
- **Quote:** “while David was pursuing (*rdp*; 30:8) the Amalekite band, the Philistines were pursuing (*dbq*; v. 2) Saul and his sons.”
- **Locus:** 31:1–2; pp. 649–650 / ~L2688–L2717
- **Targets:** [[saul]], [[jonathan]], [[philistines]], [[david]], [[1-samuel]]

### C-R8-42 | Saul’s suicide; armor-bearer; Amalekite of 2 Sam 1 is lying
- **Claim:** Battle severe; archers find Saul; he writhes in fear. Orders armor-bearer to pierce him lest uncircumcised abuse him (Samson precedent); armor-bearer refuses (very afraid). Saul falls on his own sword; armor-bearer does likewise. All die “that day together.” Contradicts Amalekite’s report 2 Sam 1:6–10—easiest explanation: Amalekite lying to curry favor with David.
- **Quote:** “This narrative contradicts the Amalekite’s report of Saul’s death in 2 Sam. 1:6–10. The easiest explanation is that the Amalekite was lying in hopes of currying favor with David.”
- **Locus:** 31:3–6; pp. 650–652 / ~L2718–L2751
- **Targets:** [[saul]], [[1-samuel]]
- **Note:** 1 Chr 10:6 “all his household” vs MT armor-bearer + all men—interdependence still moot; Chronicles more family-providence interest

### C-R8-43 | Israelites abandon cities; Philistines occupy Jezreel area
- **Claim:** Men of Israel beyond valley (N of Jezreel / Galilean hills side) and beyond Jordan abandon cities; Philistines live in them. Central hill country (Ishbosheth/Abner zone) not mentioned as lost.
- **Quote:** “the central hill country, which Saul’s son Ishbosheth and Abner would soon control, is not mentioned here.”
- **Locus:** 31:7; pp. 652–653 / ~L2752–L2763
- **Targets:** [[saul]], [[philistines]], [[1-samuel]]

### C-R8-44 | Corpse desecration: head, armor to Astartes, body on Beth-shan wall
- **Claim:** Next day Philistines strip slain; cut off Saul’s head, strip armor; send tidings to house of their idols and people (holy war of gods). Armor deposited in temple of Astartes (MT f.pl. *ʿštrwt* defended via Ugaritic plural DNs; war-goddess like Ishtar); corpse thrust on wall of Beth-shan (junction Jezreel–Gilead / Jordan Valley; Egyptian then Philistine control; temples Resheph/Antit at level V). Head presumably with armor (cf. 1 Chr 10:10).
- **Quote:** “They deposited his armor in the temple of Astartes, but his corpse they thrust on the wall of Beth-shan.”
- **Locus:** 31:8–10; pp. 653–654 / ~L2764–L2787
- **Targets:** [[saul]], [[philistines]], [[1-samuel]]
- **Note:** Extract full—do not soften desecration

### C-R8-45 | Jabesh-Gilead: night retrieval, burning, tamarisk burial, seven-day fast
- **Claim:** Jabesh-Gilead warriors (whom Saul rescued from Nahash, ch. 11) go all night, take corpses from Beth-shan wall, burn them at Jabesh (honorable here despite Amos 2:1 horror of bone-burning—Gordon: Indo-European/Hittite/Homeric parallel via Philistine custom; purpose: guarantee no re-exposure), bury bones under tamarisk, fast seven days (Ugaritic KTU 1.161 parallel). David later moves bones (2 Sam 21:12).
- **Quote:** “When the people of Jabesh-Gilead heard… they rendered kindness for kindness to Saul”
- **Locus:** 31:11–13; pp. 654–655 / ~L2788–L2799
- **Targets:** [[saul]], [[1-samuel]]

### C-R8-46 | Honorable end of tragic hero; forward to 2 Samuel elegy and messianic throne
- **Claim:** Unlike Chronicles’ guilt-focus (1 Chr 10:13–14 inquiry of ghost), 1 Sam 31 presents death with “great solemnity, even reverence” (Hertzberg). “So Saul’s life ends not in dishonour, but in honour, as befits the Lord’s anointed.” Next: David’s elegy for Saul and Jonathan—“most moving elegy in the Bible.” Book ends with Saul’s death but not the story: expectation for establishment of David’s throne, “prototype of the future King, the ‘Lord’s anointed’ (Messiah), through whom the divine plan of salvation would be fulfilled.”
- **Quote:** “So Saul’s life ends not in dishonour, but in honour, as befits the Lord’s anointed.” / “Readers would wait for the subsequent narrative with great expectation for the establishment of the throne of David, the very prototype of the future King, the ‘Lord’s anointed’ (Messiah)”
- **Locus:** 31 close; pp. 655–656 / ~L2799–L2806
- **Targets:** [[saul]], [[david]], [[jonathan]], [[kingship-in-israel]], [[1-samuel]], [[tsumura-1-samuel-nicot]]

## Coverage note
- **Lines read:** full slice R8 (source raw **13417–16224**); ~2808 lines of extracted text (chs. 23–31 complete in Tsumura’s commentary through volume close).
- **Claim count:** **46** load-bearing claims (C-R8-01 … C-R8-46).
- **Endor claims:** C-R8-26–36 (placement; anti-pagan-instrumentalization; five verbs; ʾôb expulsion; silence of legitimate media; night rite; real-Samuel/extraordinary-to-medium/God-permitted; ʾĕlōhîm; oracle of death and transfer to David; aftermath meal; solar Lady hypothesis).
- **Gilboa claims:** C-R8-41–46 (simultaneous pursuit; sons; suicide vs lying Amalekite; occupation; desecration at Beth-shan/Astartes; Jabesh honor; tragic-hero honor + messianic forward look).
- **Anointed-sparing claims:** C-R8-09–12 (En-gedi 24), C-R8-14/17–18 (Abigail restrains bloodguilt / Nabal as parallel vengeance lesson), C-R8-20–22 (Hachilah 26; deep sleep; inheritance speech).
- **Sparse-verbatim:** repetitive text-critical debates with McCarter/LXX, AXB/poetic-prose syntax notes, and place-name MR grids condensed unless load-bearing for theology or narrative structure.
- **Misc entities for integrator:** Abigail, Nabal, Achish (Ben-Maoch), medium of Endor / ʾēšet baʿălat ʾôb, Abishai, Abner, Ziklag, Ahinoam, Michal/Palti.
